items.headline: County Commission approves $350,000 animal-control contract, 5–0
items.summary: The County Commission approved a one-year, $350,000 animal-control contract with the Flagler Humane Society, voting 5–0. The vote ended a lapse in animal-control coverage of about four weeks.

items.headline: Carney elected County Commission chair, Richardson vice chair
items.summary: The County Commission unanimously elected Kim Carney as chair and Pam Richardson as vice chair at its organizational meeting.

items.headline: Palm Coast seats three new council members; Miller named vice mayor
items.summary: Three new members took their seats on the Palm Coast City Council — Amaral (District 2), Stevens (District 3) and Shelley (District 4). The council elected Ty Miller vice mayor, 4–1.

items.headline: Palm Coast passes two budget amendments
items.summary: At the same Nov. 17 meeting, the Palm Coast City Council passed two budget amendments, both unanimously.

items.headline: School Board seats new members; Ramirez elected chair, Ruddy vice chair
items.summary: At its Nov. 17 organizational meeting, the School Board seated newly elected members Moon (District 1) and Wood (District 2) alongside re-elected member Chong (District 4). The board elected Lauren Ramirez chair and Janie Ruddy vice chair.

items.headline: School Board approves $3M YMCA share unanimously
items.summary: The School Board unanimously approved the district’s $3 million share of the roughly $14 million Palm Coast YMCA planned for Town Center, on a 35-year lease.

items.headline: 2027–28 school calendar approved 4–1
items.summary: The board approved the 2027–28 school calendar 4–1, with Ruddy opposed. The calendar has 179 student days and a first day of Aug. 10.

items.headline: Planning Board recommends asphalt plant approval, 6–1
items.summary: The Palm Coast Planning Board voted 6–1 to recommend approval of the ACCI Ventures asphalt plant — 6 acres at 77 Hargrove Grade, about $6 million and roughly 45 jobs. The final decision rests with the City Council, where approval needs 4 of 5 votes.

items.headline: Flagler Beach Commission last met Nov. 12
items.summary: The Flagler Beach City Commission last met on Nov. 12, when trailer and RV parking rules (Ordinance 2026-28) were on the agenda. Its next meeting is Dec. 10.
